request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now has a "Watched total" figure (`data-testid="watched-due-total"`). It adds up the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches and shows 0.00 when they watch no one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/features/header/counters.slot.tsx`, with no server or database changes. The app already loads each user's watch list and each person's due-total, so the header adds up the people on the sheet who appear in that user's watch list. The figure is formatted the same way as the other header totals.

Each user sees only their own watches. In the test, uma watches Ada and Ben while vic sees just Ben's 4.00. Because the watch list is re-read whenever the sheet is reloaded, a user sees the updated total after reloading.
